title: Independent Voters Have More Power Down the Ballot | Vote the Whole Ballot 2026
description:
The big races get the headlines. But the ballot doesn’t stop at the top, and the decisions down the ballot can come down to a few votes.

More than 1 in 5 California voters has no party. That is real power. On the races and measures the headlines skip, independent voters are big enough to decide the outcome. If they vote the whole ballot.

Take two measures on this year’s ballot. Proposition 41 would require independent State Auditor reviews of new state special taxes every four years. Proposition 39 is California’s voter ID measure. You don’t need to belong to a party to weigh in on either one. You just need to vote.

IVP takes no position on these measures. Read both sides, then decide for yourself.

Vote the whole ballot.

A guide to California’s ballot proposals for independent-minded voters:
https://ivn.us/guide-to-californias-proposals-for-independent-minded-voters/

About IVN
Independent Voter News (IVN.us) is a nonpartisan news platform. It covers elections from the voter’s perspective, not a party’s, with data-driven reporting and verifiable sources. IVN does not endorse candidates or parties. The goal is to give voters the information they need to decide for themselves.

Election Day: Tuesday, November 3, 2026.
Learn more at IVN.us
